chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: 52nd Street stories: John Simmons, Leonard Feather and Ben Webster hitting Billie's dog
summary: Collins and Willard swap stories of Simmons and Heywood's floating rhythm section, Simmons striking Feather, and Ben Webster knocking out Billie Holiday's dog's tooth.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Shelly Manne tells about in the early '40s on the street he and --
John Simmons and Eddie Heywood had what they called a floating rhythm section. They were available for clubs, sessions, after hours, any time anybody needed a rhythm section they went as a unit.

Well, I was probably -- no, I was probaby in the army then, you know. But at this time it was Sid John Simmons, Syd Catlett, and they would always work with Ben also Bill Webster, alto. That's when John Simmons and Leonard Feather got into this thing. I think John knocked Leonard down, I don't know. Something.
On a street corner, I understood!

Yeah, yeah. And that's also the time of Lady Day had this dog, boxer, which -- let's see, his name was Mister, and she was walking -- we were at rehearsal this day, and Ben was out in the street, and Lady asked Ben to hold Mister while she went inside or something, so he was holding Mister. And Mister kept jumping up and jumping on him and trying to bite him and Ben hit Mister in the mouth and knocked his tooth out. So Billy came out, you know what happened. She called him everything.
